A1.justification: Both PDFs are complete, readable 16-page versions of the same VideoMindPalace study. Their main text, equations, tables, figures and appendix Sections 7-10 support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original VideoMindPalace benchmark evaluations, qualitative examples and appendix ablations, including experimental outcomes in Tables 1-5.

after.justification: v2 retains the original benchmark evaluations and appendix ablation outcomes in Tables 1-5. These remain original empirical results.

M1.justification: Sections 3 and 8 retain the same object tracking, activity-zone discovery, three-layer semantic graph construction and LLM querying procedures. No method component or procedural adaptation changes.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate NExT-QA, EgoSchema, IntentQA, AMB and VMB. VMB retains the same EPIC-KITCHENS/Ego-4D sources and spatial, temporal, layout and open-ended task coverage.

E2.justification: Comparator membership matches within every reported comparison. This includes IG-VLM, LLoVi, VideoTree and VideoAgent on VMB; S-QA and AMEGO remain in the AMB comparison, and LLoVi remains in appendix Table 5.

E3.justification: Both retain the same evaluation settings, including EgoSchema validation evaluation, multiple-choice accuracy, 0-5 open-ended scoring, GPT-4 primary results, VMB sample sizes and duration categories, and appendix ablation controls.

E4.justification: Appendix Section 9 retains the location-clustering versus temporal-window ablation and the GPT-3.5/GPT-4 analysis. The qualitative cases and graph-based reasoning examples in Figures 3-4 are also unchanged.

E5.justification: Both use the same point-estimate reporting. Neither reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests; appendix Section 10.2 describes dataset composition rather than experimental uncertainty.

E6.justification: All numerical entries in Tables 1-5 match. For example, VideoMindPalace retains 75.8 on NExT-QA, 68.6 on EgoSchema, 70.1 on IntentQA, 37.8 total on AMB and 3.8 for VMB open-ended QA. Qualitative findings also match.

T1.justification: The hierarchical graph definitions, similarity and distance equations (1)-(2), and appendix Section 8.2's edge definitions and distance normalization are unchanged. No mathematical argument or proof is added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution bullets and conclusion retain the same claims about environment-grounded hierarchical video representation, the VMB benchmark and effectiveness across video QA benchmarks.

C2.justification: Both retain the interpretations concerning reduced redundancy and structured LLM reasoning, the AMB visual-to-text query error explanation, and limitations concerning propagated perception errors and missing object color or texture.

D1.justification: The model and tracker choices, QA prompts, graph thresholds, 1-fps query-construction procedure and human annotation checks in Sections 5, 8 and 10.1 are unchanged. No implementation or code/data access information is added.

R1.justification: Section 2 and the bibliography retain the same cited works and research positioning, including the relationships to scene-graph approaches, VideoTree, VideoAgent and AMEGO.

P1.justification: v2 adds Yiqiu Ren to the author list and updates the arXiv version/date stamp. Apart from minor spacing and typesetting differences, the scientific wording, terminology, section order and appendix organization are unchanged.

P2.justification: Figures 1-5 and Tables 1-5 retain the same content, captions, structure and placement. The page organization is preserved, with no figure/table redesign or layout reorganization.

improvement.justification: The revision updates authorship and version information, with minor typesetting differences. The scientific argument, empirical evidence, reproducibility details and acknowledged limitations remain unchanged throughout the main text and appendices, leaving overall paper quality essentially unchanged.
